svg.title: Separate gateway, residual, and private-endpoint paths
svg.desc: The first route carries gateway-supported HTTPS through Arc proxy, an enterprise proxy when configured, Azure Arc gateway, and the supported service endpoint. The second keeps residual public destinations on their required direct or enterprise-proxy path outside the gateway tunnel. The third reaches a supported service private endpoint over private routing with the required DNS. Arc Private Link Scopes remain unsupported for Azure Local.
svg.text: Separate gateway, residual, and private-endpoint paths
Read each numbered route left to right. These are route classes, not one universal proxy configuration.
An enterprise proxy, when used, is an additional hop; Arc gateway does not replace all proxy policy.
2. Residual public dependencies: outside the gateway tunnel
Keep the applicable regional, bootstrap, certificate, OEM, and workload dependencies reachable.
Private transport does not make every destination private or remove all public service dependencies.
Azure Arc Private Link Scopes are unsupported for Azure Local; required Arc DNS names resolve publicly.
Cloud gatewayBypass skips the tunnel, not the enterprise proxy. Local proxy bypass is a separate setting.
